intended_object: The point reflection through a point p of a topological additive torsor P, i.e. the map q ↦ (p -ᵥ q) +ᵥ p (in a vector space, q ↦ 2p − q), packaged as a self-homeomorphism of P. Inferred from the docstring "`Equiv.pointReflection` as a homeomorphism".
explanation:
The definition composes `Homeomorph.constVSub p` (q ↦ p -ᵥ q) with `Homeomorph.vaddConst p` (v ↦ v +ᵥ p). The composite sends q to (p -ᵥ q) +ᵥ p, which is exactly `Equiv.pointReflection p` (see `pointReflection_apply`). It is built the same way as the existing versions: `Equiv.pointReflection`, `AffineEquiv.pointReflection`, `ContinuousAffineEquiv.pointReflection` and `AffineIsometryEquiv.pointReflection`.

The only assumptions are an additive group V acting as a torsor on P, with both carrying topologies that make the torsor operations continuous (`IsTopologicalAddTorsor`). That is the minimal setting in which the reflection is a homeomorphism, so this is the natural generality.

The surrounding section declares a multiplicative `Torsor` variable, but the definition binds its own additive variables and does not use it. `Equiv.pointReflection` is itself only defined for additive torsors, so having no multiplicative version does not make this definition too narrow.
